narratives.Description: Prove the core cold-clone reconstitution scenario end-to-end with an explicit executable acceptance test: a fresh clone of a hybrid consumer in a mismatched sandbox where both `.deft/core/` (content) and `.deft/.cli/` (engine) are gitignored and therefore absent must reach a ready-to-use state with zero manual steps. The test drives the ordered flow -- read the committed package.json pin, run the global-first ladder, run update to re-project `.deft/core/` and stamp VERSION, resolve USER.md, then run session:start + verify -- and asserts the reconstitution trace, the registry-down hard-fail message, and the matched-env short-circuit.
narratives.Overview:
Part of epic #2203 (resolves the M1 gap).

## Summary

Prove the core cold-clone reconstitution scenario end-to-end: a fresh `git clone` of a hybrid consumer in a mismatched sandbox, where both `.deft/core/` and `.deft/.cli/` are gitignored (so NEITHER content nor engine is present on clone), reaches a ready-to-use state with zero manual steps.

## The ordered flow under test

```text
1. read committed pin from package.json          (always present in git)
2. global-first ladder (#child A):
     global engine? -> else local .deft/.cli? -> else install (npm i -g OR npm install --prefix .deft/.cli/<platform>)
3. run `update` -> engine re-projects .deft/core/ (content), stamps VERSION
4. USER.md resolution (#child H)
5. proceed: framework-local gates now runnable
```

This is the scenario the whole epic exists to make work; it must be an explicit, executable acceptance test, not an assumption.

## Acceptance criteria

- A simulated cold clone (both dirs absent) reconstitutes engine + content and runs `session:start` + `verify:*` with zero manual npm/PATH/`DEFT_USER_PATH` steps.
- The reconstitution trace is emitted and asserted (ties to #child A structured trace).
- Registry-down path hard-fails with the "stage this" message rather than hanging or failing open.
- Matched-env clone (engine already global) short-circuits the ladder at step 1/2 with no reinstall.

## Related

Parent #2203. Integration test spanning #child A, #child C, #child H.
narratives.UserStory: As a Directive maintainer guarding the cold-clone adoption path, I want an executable end-to-end acceptance test that simulates a fresh clone with both .deft/core and .deft/.cli absent and drives the full reconstitution flow through the global-first ladder and update and USER.md resolution, so that the scenario the whole epic exists to make work is proven automatically instead of assumed and any regression fails CI.
narratives.ImplementationPlan:
1. Add a new acceptance test `packages/core/src/resolution/cold-clone-reconstitution.test.ts` that builds a simulated cold-clone fixture (a temp dir with a committed package.json pin but NO `.deft/core/` and NO `.deft/.cli/`) using injected seams so no real network/npm runs. If shared setup is non-trivial, factor it into a small colocated `packages/core/src/resolution/reconstitution-harness.ts` (+ its own test) that wires the fixture + seams.
2. Drive the ordered flow against the merged spine: read the pin, run the global-first ladder (`resolution/engine-ladder.ts::resolveEngine`), run update re-projection (`init-deposit/refresh.ts::runRefreshDepositCli`) to reconstitute `.deft/core/` + stamp VERSION, resolve USER.md via the merged `user-config/resolve-user-md.ts`, then assert framework-local gates (session:start + verify) become runnable -- all with zero manual npm/PATH/DEFT_USER_PATH steps.
3. Assert the structured reconstitution trace emitted by the keystone ladder (ties to #2264's trace); assert the registry-down seam hard-fails with the canonical `stage this` message (never hangs / fails open); assert a matched-env fixture (engine already global) short-circuits the ladder at step 1/2 with no reinstall.
4. Consume the merged modules read-only via injected seams; do NOT modify the keystone resolution spine, refresh, or user-config production code -- this is an acceptance test that pins current behavior. If a genuine seam gap blocks the test, add the MINIMAL testability seam and note it.
5. Run `task ts:check-lane`, `pnpm exec vitest run packages/core/src/resolution`, and `task check:framework-source`. Add a brief CHANGELOG entry.
